In English, a single personal pronoun th.why: A firm rule of English case, used constantly ('with him', 'for her', 'sit with me') and stated in every grammar of English; the subject forms after a preposition are rare errors. Bare plural pairs like 'with he' cannot be counted (the tokens also match 'with heavy', 'with health'), so it is counted on longer frames. 'Stand by I' (138) and 'Lean on I' (21) are hits such as 'Stand by I'll report back' or 'Lean on IRL support', not the sentence with a subject pronoun.

notes: Mirrors grammar-replace-0020: the original rule is removed. New members reach the answer only through it (does not know). A fixed phrase stored whole keeps its form (nothing needs to give way under a delete); one built from the rule loses it. A case rule, for variety: the topic's other TBox rules are verb agreement (0005, 0006, 0019), letter case (0007) and number in compounds (0008). New relation `takes_case_form` (functional: a class of positions takes one case form). Restricted to a single pronoun: coordinated ones ('between you and I') are a known hypercorrection and kept out of every prompt, as are 'than' and 'but', whose status as prepositions is disputed ('taller than I'). Determinate queries use neopronouns (ze/hir, xe/xem): real but rare, and the prompt states each one's object form, so the model knows nothing about the member but its forms and its position, and the rule is the only route. World structure (coordinator's rule, README Decisions 2): in a world where a fixed phrase is stored whole, the phrase's class membership gives way and it falls under a wider, unedited rule that still gives the original form; it never stands as an exception to the edited rule, which would be the inconsistent patch. The two phrases are independent storage choices, so four worlds. Under delete, the wider rule would re-derive the deleted one, so the delete record's worlds also cut the class's link to it (README, Delete under determinacy: the wider rule itself cannot go, being anchored by countless instances outside the chain). In the stored worlds 'stand by' and 'lean on' are read as phrasal verbs (to support, to rely on), with 'me' as their direct object rather than the object of a preposition: grammars do treat prepositional verbs as units (Quirk et al. call the noun phrase a 'prepositional object', and they passivise: 'He was stood by'), so the membership can really give way, and the object of a verb still takes its object form (a rule this edit leaves alone). 'Sit with me' was not used as a member: 'with' has no phrasal-verb reading there. Choosing a case form for a class of positions is a class inclusion with one filler: dl. Near unrelated asks the object of a verb ('us'), so a model that overgeneralises the edit to every object answers 'we' and is caught.
